36. MongoDB's ASP Product Team maintains a public example repository, `mongodb/ASP_example`, described as both a human-readable corpus and a RAG-optimised repository for code generation. Its canonical processor format is a JSON structure beginning with `{ "$source": { ... } }`. ([GitHub, mongodb/ASP_example](https://github.com/mongodb/ASP_example))

1. `$source` specifies the connection a stream processor streams data from, and is the ingestion point of the pipeline. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-source/ 2. `$source` must be the first stage of any pipeline it appears in. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-source/ 3. A pipeline may contain at most one `$source` stage. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-source/ 4. Once `$source` has ingested a document, ordinary MongoDB aggregation stages may transform it downstream. — https://www.mongodb

11. `timeField` designates an authoritative event timestamp for each ingested message, and its value must be a `$toDate` or `$dateFromString` expression — not a bare field path. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-source/ 12. If `timeField` is omitted, ASP derives the timestamp from the source message's own timestamp; for Kafka this is the broker receipt time. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-source/ (default behavior) ; the Kafka-broker specialization is a secondary-source claim from https://medium.com/mongodb/mongodb-atlas-st

6. `timeField` sets the authoritative event timestamp and accepts only a `$toDate` or `$dateFromString` expression over a source field. When omitted, the source's own message timestamp is used. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-source/ 7. Watermarks are applied only when the pipeline contains `$tumblingWindow`, `$hoppingWindow`, or `$sessionWindow`; a watermark advances only when a document arrives with an event time later than any previously consumed document. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/architecture/ 8. **F3 — Choosing a `$source` variant silently fixes your recovery story, not just your input.** A Kafka `$source` gives replayable offsets bounded by topic retention but **forfeits the built-in failover processor** (C69, C79). A change-stream `$source` gets failover but a hard recovery ceiling at the oplog window (C42, C73, C79). A Kinesis or cron `$source` also forfeits failover (C79). This coupling is stated nowhere in one place in the vendor docs; `practice.md` derived it and the other three reports supply its components.

This report covers only the `$source` aggregation stage of MongoDB Atlas Stream Processing and the set of source forms it accepts (Apache Kafka, MongoDB change streams at collection / database / cluster scope, AWS Kinesis, inline document arrays, cron schedules). It traces when each form appeared and identifies the primary and official sources for each.

9. The 31 July 2025 release added Initial Sync to `$source` when reading from Atlas collections, letting a processor ingest pre-existing documents as synthetic `insert` change events before tailing the change stream. ([MongoDB Docs, Changelog](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/changelog/); field semantics in [MongoDB Docs, `$source` Stage](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-source/))

18. The Kafka form takes `connectionName` and `topic` as required fields, with optional `timeField`, `partitionIdleTimeout` (`size` + `unit`), `schemaRegistry.connectionName`, and a `config` sub-document carrying `auto_offset_reset` (default `"latest"`), `group_id` (auto-generated as `asp-${streamProcessorId}-consumer` when omitted), `enable_auto_commit`, `keyFormat` (default `"binData"`), and `keyFormatError` (`"dlq"` or `"passThrough"`). ([MongoDB Docs, `$source` Stage](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-source/))

23. The Kinesis form requires `connectionName`, `stream`, and `config.consumerARN`; `region` is required when the stream name exists in more than one region. Optional fields are `timeField`, `tsFieldName`, `shardIdleTimeout`, `config.initialPosition` (default `"LATEST"`), `config.atTimestamp`, and `config.reshardDetectionIntervalSecs` (default `300`). ([MongoDB Docs, `$source` Stage](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-source/); syntax block reproduced in [MongoDB Blog, 2026-01-07](https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/technical/announcing-kinesis-support-for-mongo

25. The document-array form takes a `documents` array (or an expression evaluating to one) and must not be combined with `connectionName`. It is the form used for local testing with `sp.process()`. ([MongoDB Docs, `$source` Stage](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-source/))

27. The cron form departs from standard cron semantics: when both day of month and day of week are restricted, a document is emitted only when **both** conditions match, whereas conventional cron implementations use OR. ([MongoDB Docs, `$source` Stage](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-source/))

**F4 — `$source` is immutable in practice, and this is the most-corroborated non-obvious fact in the run.** All four reports independently reached C75 while citing **three different documentation pages** ([S2] architecture, [S3] limitations, [S9] manage-stream-processor). The practical consequence: iterate on source configuration with ephemeral `sp.process()` runs against a `documents` array before promoting (C7). The one apparent exception is X6, which is unresolved.

**D5 — The `$source` immutability rule and the failover procedure point in opposite directions.** Claim #23 says the `$source` stage cannot be modified while `resumeFromCheckpoint=true`. The failover procedure instructs operators to restart primary processors with `config.startAtOperationTime` set to the timestamp at which the failover processor stopped — which is a `$source.config` change. The documentation does not state whether the failover path implies `resumeFromCheckpoint=false`, whether `startAtOperationTime` is exempt from the immutability rule, or whether operators are expected to rec

- C75: the `$source` stage cannot be modified while `resumeFromCheckpoint=true` [S9]. - The failover procedure [S7] instructs operators to restart primary processors with `config.startAtOperationTime` set to the timestamp at which the failover processor stopped — which **is** a `$source.config` change. - The documentation does not state whether the failover path implies `resumeFromCheckpoint=false`, whether `startAtOperationTime` is exempt, or whether operators must recreate the processor. - **Unresolved:** the mechanics of applying `startAtOperationTime` to an existing checkpointed processor.

3. Atlas Stream Processing requires documents in the source data stream to be valid JSON or EJSON. Documents that fail this check go to the dead letter queue if one is configured. ([MongoDB Docs, `$source` Stage](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-source/))

22. A pipeline cannot use `$hoppingWindow`, `$sessionWindow`, or `$tumblingWindow` when `initialSync` is enabled on the `$source`. ([MongoDB Docs, `$source` Stage](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-source/))

29. When the default `resumeFromCheckpoint=true` is in effect, the `$source` stage of a running processor cannot be modified. ([MongoDB Docs, Limitations](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/limitations/))

31. Kafka `$source` stages are subject to per-tier partition limits. Exceeding the stream processing workspace tier's partition limit fails the processor and requires a tier upgrade. ([MongoDB Docs, Limitations](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/limitations/))

Documentation written before the rename describes the same `$source` against differently named containers. ([Terraform Registry, Stream Instance to Stream Workspace migration guide](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/MongoDB/mongodbatlas/latest/docs/guides/stream-instance-to-stream-workspace-migration-guide))

A disconfirming search was run and produced real results: the documented limitations (claims 29–35), the Pub/Sub source/sink asymmetry, the cron form's non-standard day-of-month/day-of-week semantics and absence of cost savings, and the stale third-party enumeration in disagreement 2.

The caveat is disagreement 3: source *independence* is partial. `infoworld.com` and `oneuptime.com` are editorially independent of MongoDB, but only InfoWorld is non-derivative, and it contributes nothing beyond the GA date. All substantive technical claims rest on MongoDB's own primary documentation, which is authoritative for a proprietary service but cannot be externally corroborated.

52. Checkpoints record source offsets, not copies of source documents: oplog resume tokens for change-stream sources, partition offsets for Kafka sources. Restarting a processor queries the last committed checkpoint and resumes from the state it describes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/architecture/ 54. This report covers the `$source` stage of Atlas Stream Processing pipelines: the source variants it exposes, their configuration surface, the operational behaviour that follows from choosing one, and the failure modes practitioners must plan for. It stays inside the `$source` stage. Sink stages (`$emit`, `$merge`), window stages, `$validate`, `$lookup`, and the Atlas Stream Processing platform as a whole are out of scope except where a `$source` field's meaning depends on them (watermarks, checkpoints, DLQ).

29. `initialSync.enable: true` makes `$source` first emit every pre-existing document as an `insert` change event before switching to live change events, which is the built-in backfill-then-stream path. `initialSync.parallelism` defaults to `1`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-source/ 30. `initialSync` cannot be combined with `$hoppingWindow`, `$sessionWindow`, or `$tumblingWindow`; the collection list is fixed at processor start and new collections are not picked up; and a sync failure on any one listed collection fails the whole processor. — https://www.mo

42. Atlas Stream Processing does not scale horizontally and uses a single core for transformation stages except where a stage takes a `parallelism` value. `$source` parallelism (via `initialSync.parallelism`) is pooled with `$lookup`, `$merge`, `$emit`, and `$externalFunction` against a per-tier cumulative budget; exceeding it is an error that requires a tier upgrade or lower parallelism. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/limitations/ · https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-source/ 43. 6. `$source` is polymorphic: its accepted field set depends on the kind of source, and the documented kinds are Apache Kafka topics, MongoDB collection change streams, MongoDB database change streams, MongoDB cluster-wide change streams, AWS Kinesis data streams, an inline document array, and a cron schedule. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-source/ 7. The vendor's own material supplies its own counterweights — the documented limitations, the Pub/Sub source/sink asymmetry (C86), the cron form's non-standard day semantics (C59) and absence of cost savings (C62), and the internal inconsistencies at X4, X6 and X10.
